x: B is correct (UPPSC 2010 key). Assertion A is true: the RTI Act has raised the sense of responsibility in the bureaucracy. Reason R is also true: there are still miles to go. But R does not explain why responsibility has risen, so option A (R explains A) is wrong; C and D each wrongly call one statement false.

C is correct: clogging offices with indiscriminate demands is misuse by applicants. A is wrong because excessive, bad-faith use of Section 8 is misuse by public authorities; B and D are wrong because personal disputes, blackmail and private disputes are misuse by applicants, not authorities.

A is the incorrect statement: in May 2026 the CIC held that BCCI is NOT a public authority under Section 2(h), as it is not substantially financed by government. B, C and D are correct: the CIC held in 2010 that the Rajiv Gandhi Foundation was not a public authority, the Delhi HC dismissed the 2011 plea for non-appearance, and the CIC ordered CBSE to disclose answer-book tender data withheld under 8(1)(e).

A is correct: eSeva (2001) set up integrated citizen service centres for bills and certificates. B is wrong: MeeSeva came in 2011 as single-window G2C centres, while online tendering was e-Procurement (2003). C and D pair the initiatives with wrong years and purposes.

A is correct: NeSDA (National e-Services Delivery Assessment) is a DARPG tool from 2019. B is wrong: the State Collaboration Initiatives scheme was revised in 2015-16, not launched after 2021. C is wrong: the Citizen's Charter portal is an executive tool, not a constitutional amendment. D is wrong: CPGRAMS is DARPG's grievance system, not a World Bank index.

D is correct: all four statements are true. NITI Aayog (2015) is non-constitutional and non-statutory, is the apex public policy think tank, is chaired by the Prime Minister and works on cooperative federalism.
D is correct: all four are true. BHIM was launched on UPI on 30 December 2016, PRAGATI on 25 March 2015, Dial.Gov in December 2012, and e-Taal is run by NIC.

B is correct: a member of a Public Service Commission can be removed for misbehaviour only after an inquiry by the Supreme Court. A, C and D are wrong because neither the Chief Minister, nor the Governor without inquiry, nor the Lok Sabha Speaker by a vote can remove a PSC member.

D is correct: all three are true. The Supreme Court agreed (Aug 2026) to examine the DPDP-RTI conflict over Section 8(1)(j); the Economic Survey 2025-26 called for 're-examination' of RTI; and it floated a possible ministerial veto over draft policy discussions and service records.
